items.stem: A registrar's sheet has one row per student, with the columns ID number, name and program. How does a data model describe this sheet?

options.text: Student is the entity, the columns are attributes, and each row is an instance.
options.feedback: The entity is the kind of thing the school keeps data about. Attributes describe it, and each row is one example.

options.text: The ID number is the entity, because it is what identifies each row.
options.feedback: The ID number is a fact about a student, so it is an attribute. It helps tell instances apart, but the thing being described is the student.

options.text: Each row is an entity and each column is an instance of that entity.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed. A column is an attribute, and a row is one instance of the entity.

options.text: Maria Santos is an entity, because she is a real person in the school.
options.feedback: Maria Santos is one student, which makes her an instance. The entity is the kind of thing, Student.

items.stem: A scheduling system records the room where each class meets, such as SOM 407. The registrar also wants each room's capacity and whether it has a projector, and wants to list everything scheduled in one room. Should Room be an attribute of Class or an entity?

options.text: An entity, because a room has facts of its own and is shared.
options.feedback: Capacity and projector describe the room, and one room hosts many classes. Both are signs that Room needs its own table.

options.text: An attribute, because a room is only a name such as SOM 407.
options.feedback: A name is enough only if nothing else is recorded about the room. Here the room has its own facts, so it needs to be an entity.

options.text: An attribute, because rooms rarely change.
options.feedback: How often something changes does not decide this. What matters is whether the thing has facts of its own and is shared by many records.

options.text: An entity only if the school has more than 100 rooms.
options.feedback: The number of rooms does not decide it. One room with its own facts is already an entity.

items.stem: A student enrolls in ITENT 45 on 12 August and later receives a grade. Where should the enrollment date and the grade be stored?

options.text: In an Enrollment entity that links the student and the course.
options.feedback: The date and the grade describe the pairing of one student with one course, so the pairing is an entity.

options.text: As attributes of Student, because the student receives the grade.
options.feedback: A student has many courses and would then need many grades. The grade belongs to one student in one course.

options.text: As attributes of Course, because the course gives the grade.
options.feedback: A course has many students, each with a different grade. The grade cannot be a single value on the course.

options.text: In both Student and Course so either one can be looked up.
options.feedback: Storing the same fact in two places lets the copies disagree. A separate Enrollment entity stores it once.
